t: This is Albemarle Street, a Mayfair street off Piccadilly, known for its art galleries and for Brown's Hotel at number 33. Lord Byron's publisher, John Murray, was based here. Oscar Wilde belonged to the Albemarle Club, where an insult led him to sue for libel and, in the end, to prison. Several aristocrats were born or died on this street. Lieutenant-General John Huske died here, and so did James Scott, Earl of Dalkeith, a grandson of Charles II. Edward Harbord, the 3rd Baron Suffield, a politician and abolitionist, was born here.
